plate.purpose: One step above the room: tool stacks, code blocks and the composer. Daylight: #F7F9FC.

display.purpose: The Nerve wordmark only: Geist at 700 weight with -0.03em tracking, followed by the 12x17 fleet pane.

nameplate.purpose: The open session's agent name in the chat header: Geist at 1.2rem, 700 weight, -0.02em, in its family hue.

name.purpose: Agent and speaker names in the chat header, top-level session rows and message headers. The operator's name takes Cantaloupe text.

headline.purpose: Section titles on settings and dialog surfaces.

title.purpose: Panel header labels, field labels, Send, table heads. Sentence case.

body.purpose: Agent prose on the 72em reading measure (about 140 characters, which is the whole column on most screens).

ui.purpose: Chips, list rows, inputs, toolbar buttons and tree entries.

label.purpose: Status bar, metadata, hints, badges and intermediate assistant messages.

mono.purpose: Tool rows, timestamps, durations, model names and code; tabular numerals always on.

shadows.name: plate-shadow
shadows.purpose: Edge light on every plate, tool stack and the active segmented chip. Daylight: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border).

shadows.name: plate-shadow-operator
shadows.purpose: Warm edge light on the operator's message plate. Daylight: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-operator) 45%, var(--border)).

shadows.name: float-shadow
shadows.purpose: The composer and the command palette shell: the only surfaces that float. Daylight: 0 14px 36px rgba(19, 23, 34, 0.14), 0 1px 2px rgba(19, 23, 34, 0.08), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border).

shadows.name: menu-shadow
shadows.purpose: Inline select listboxes, slash menus and top bar panels.

shadows.name: pane-edge
shadows.purpose: The window frame of a dark pane; removed when the pane lights.

shadows.name: Bloom
shadows.purpose: The light a lit pane throws on the ground in its own colour (live 62%, operator 58%, error 58%). Daylight sets it to none.

motion.name: switch-duration
motion.purpose: Every state switch: pane colour, hover fill, border colour, Send brightness. Never looped.

motion.name: switch-ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve, used for switches and entrances alike.

motion.name: enter-fast
motion.purpose: Fade or slide-down entrance for search bars and menus.

motion.name: enter-message
motion.purpose: Opacity fade when a message enters the transcript.

motion.name: enter-drawer
motion.purpose: Settings drawer slide-in from the right.

motion.name: send-pulse
motion.purpose: Send flashes brighter once when a message leaves.

motion.name: streaming-cursor
motion.purpose: The only looping animation: a small live pane at the end of streaming text. Stopped under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion makes every switch and entrance instant.

motion.name: arrive-ease
motion.purpose: Arrivals: drawers, menus, the lifted chip crossing its track. A confident deceleration, never a bounce.

motion.name: light-delay
motion.purpose: Light travels: a state arrives at the fleet pane first, then the chat header, the agents column and the transcript gutter, one region per 70ms. Lights go out together.

motion.name: view-switch
motion.purpose: Chat and Tasks switch as a view transition with the lifted chip as the shared element.

motion.name: composer-handoff
motion.purpose: On send the composer lifts 3px and settles as the turn leaves it and lands in the transcript.

breakpoints.name: topbar-compact
breakpoints.purpose: Below this chips and icon buttons drop to a 40px minimum.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: controls grow to a 44px touch minimum and inputs use 16px text.

breakpoints.name: compact-layout
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: the three columns collapse to one with panel toggles in the top bar.

components.name: Pane
components.description: The signature state marker: a flat lit rectangle in four states (off, live, operator, error) and two sizes (10x14, 8x11). It switches in 120ms and never pulses. With an identity hue the off state tints its glass (56% hue into Pane Off, 62% into the frame); lit states ignore the hue.

narrative.overview:
An operator's console is a building seen at night. You do not read the facade by its architecture; you read it by which rooms are lit and how warm the light is. Nerve borrows that reading. Cold electric blue is an agent at work. Warm cantaloupe is the operator, and anything that has finished and now waits on the operator. When work is done the window goes back to its family colour: every room keeps its own light on at idle, and only a lit pane blooms, which is how work shows. Colour never decorates, it reports, and because every lit surface means something, the shell can hold a whole fleet in a glance without asking for attention.

The mood is midnight, exact, calm, dense, lit. This is an Operate-mode surface that stays open for hours, so the brand lives in precise details rather than expression: a 28px row unit shared by every list row, tool row and panel header; plates that read by value and a 1px edge light instead of drawn borders; one display face reserved for the wordmark and the names of agents and speakers; prose held to a measure that spans the column. Density is welcome because nothing pulses, glows or gradients. State changes are a light switch, 120ms, on or off.

The system refuses the hacker costume (scanlines, glowing HUD chrome, tracked uppercase labels), the grey dashboard with one decorative accent, glass and gradients, coloured side rails, and any pulsing or breathing motion. Daylight is the same building by day: cool paper, printed hairlines instead of edge light, panes printed as ink swatches, identical meanings. The previous appearance survives only as an opt-in Classic skin scoped under its own attribute and is not part of this system.
keyCharacteristics: Light temperature is the state vocabulary: blue works, cantaloupe waits on you, red failed, dark is done.
Panes are the state marker: an idle pane shows its family colour at 84% strength, a lit pane switches to the state colour and casts a short bloom; no dots, rails or glyph icons.
One 28px row unit across list rows, tool rows, panel headers and the status bar; the top bar is 44px.
Raised plates read by tonal value plus a 1px top edge light; only floating surfaces cast a real offset shadow.
Corners stay between 1px and 4px; larger radius steps clamp to 4px.
Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for reading and UI, Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular numerals for measures, Geist for names only.
Sentence case everywhere; no eyebrows, kickers or tracked caps.
Motion is a 120ms switch with a near-linear ease-out; a new turn lands with one 200ms rise; reduced motion makes both instant.
The composer is the operator's next window: a dark plate with a dark gutter pane at rest, warmed to the operator plate with a lit pane while the operator is in it.
The shell is a Midnight frame around one lifted Panel room with a 6px reveal; tool stacks, code and the composer step up once more to Plate.

rules.name: The Light Temperature Rule
rules.body: Blue is agent work, cantaloupe is the operator and anything waiting on the operator, red is error, and nothing else is coloured. A surface that is not reporting one of those three states is a neutral. Family hues are identity, not state: they sit on idle panes, on names, on the header band and on the open row, and a pane that is lit always shows the state colour with its bloom. A cron row's pane carries the job's light: Electric Blue while a run is in flight, Signal Red while an enabled job's last run stands broken, off otherwise; a skipped run is quiet, not broken. A task's pane on the board follows the same rule: Electric Blue while its agent runs, Signal Red when the run broke, Cantaloupe while it waits in Review for the operator, off otherwise.

rules.name: The Identity Rule
rules.body: Every agent family owns one of seven hues (main is pinned to Cantaloupe; children take a lighter shade of their root's hue), assigned on first sight and operator-pickable from a root row. The hue stays on at idle: 84% of it fills the family's off panes (70% in the frame), the agent's name takes it in the display face (darkened 42% toward ink in Daylight), the chat header band takes a 9% tint (14% in Daylight) and the open room's row a 14% tint over Raised. Electric Blue is never an identity hue, and a lit pane always shows the state colour, so identity and state never trade places. On the Tasks board the assignee's family hue sits in the glass of the task's off pane and colours the assignee's name.

rules.name: The Window Rule
rules.body: The composer is the operator's next window. At rest it is a dark plate with a dark pane in the gutter; while the operator is in it (focus, or text already typed) it warms to Operator Plate with the warm edge light and the pane lights Cantaloupe, so the turn being written looks like the turns already sent. The side-column editors (memory section, config file) are windows too: Plate at rest, Operator Plate with the warm edge light and a lit Cantaloupe pane in their status line while the operator types; no focus ring, no drawn border. The login page is the first window: the brand pane lit Cantaloupe over the sign, and one floating password window that warms while the operator is in it.

rules.name: The Names Rule
rules.body: Geist is used only for the wordmark and for agent or speaker names. Headings, labels and buttons stay in Atkinson.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, header, chip and button is sentence case. No eyebrows, no kickers above headings, no letterspaced capitals.

rules.name: The One Row Rule
rules.body: Every list row, tool row, panel header and the status bar sits on the 1.867rem (28px) row unit; density comes from sharing one rhythm, not from shrinking it.

rules.name: The Edge Light Rule
rules.body: Plates read by value and a 1px top highlight, not by drawn borders; Daylight prints a hairline instead. Drawn borders are reserved for inputs, outline buttons and hairline dividers.

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: The shell is a dark frame around one lifted room. Top bar, side columns and status bar sit flat on Midnight with hairlines only; the centre column is a single plate of Panel with the edge light and 4px corners, and the frame shows for 6px around it. Surfaces inside the room step up once more to Plate.

rules.name: The Switch Rule
rules.body: State changes switch in 120ms with `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`; nothing breathes or pulses, and reduced motion makes every transition and animation instant. Entrances (messages, menus, drawers) fade or slide once in 140ms to 220ms using the same ease. A new turn in the transcript lands with one 200ms rise of 6px and a fade, and that is the transcript's only entrance. Light travels: when a run starts, the fleet pane comes on first, the chat header 70ms later, the agents column at 140ms and the transcript gutter at 210ms; lights go out together. Arrivals use the arrive ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) at 180ms to 260ms, never a bounce. The Chat and Tasks switch is a view transition (chip slides across its track in 220ms, room cross-fades in 160ms); on send the composer lifts 3px and settles in 220ms.

rules.name: The Bloom Rule
rules.body: A lit pane casts a short bloom of its own colour, and that is the only light in the system that spreads: off panes, plates, buttons and text never glow. The bloom switches on and off with the pane in 120ms. Daylight prints panes flat.

dos: **Do** keep an agent family's hue on at idle: its panes at 84%, its name, the header band and the open row; lit panes always show the state colour with its bloom (The Identity Rule).

**Do** show state only with a lit pane: Electric Blue for agent work, Cantaloupe for the operator and work waiting on the operator, Signal Red for failure, Pane Off when done (The Light Temperature Rule).
**Do** switch panes and hover fills in 120ms with `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` and let reduced motion make them instant (The Switch Rule).

**Do** warm the composer to Operator Plate and light its gutter pane while the operator is in it, on focus or with text typed, so the turn being written matches the turns already sent (The Window Rule).
**Do** let a new turn land with one 200ms rise and fade on the switch ease; the transcript has no other entrance.

**Do** build raised surfaces as plates: Panel for the room, Plate inside it, each with the 1px edge light and no drawn border; in Daylight the token prints a hairline (The Edge Light Rule, The Frame Rule).
**Do** keep every list row, tool row, panel header and the status bar on the 1.867rem row unit (The One Row Rule).
**Do** reserve Geist for the wordmark and agent or speaker names (The Names Rule).
**Do** hold agent prose to the 72em reading measure and let code, tables and charts take the column.
**Do** set timestamps, counts, durations, models and code in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular numerals.
**Do** keep corners between 1px and 4px; 6px is only for the floating command palette shell.
**Do** make Send the one warm control on a screen: Cantaloupe fill, Midnight label, 3px radius.
**Do** give every pane without adjacent text an accessible label (Running, Waiting on you, Failed, Idle).
**Do** let light travel: stagger a state's arrival by region (fleet pane, chat header, agents column, transcript gutter, 70ms apart) and never by element; lights go out together.
**Do** move chrome on the arrive ease (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, 180ms to 260ms) and switch views with a view transition; no bounce, no elastic curves.
**Do** treat the side-column editors as operator windows: Plate at rest, Operator Plate with a lit status-line pane while the operator types, never a focus ring (The Window Rule).
**Do** let a cron row's pane carry the job's light: blue in flight, red while an enabled job stands broken, off otherwise; a skipped run stays quiet.

**Do** keep the Settings drawer a flat Panel plate with the edge light and no blur; rows separate by hairlines, selects sit flat on Raised, and the switch thumb is a pane that lights Cantaloupe when on.
**Do** keep the Tasks board flat: lanes separated by hairlines, tasks as rows on Plate with the edge light, priority and run state as words; the pane is the only coloured element besides a lit word.
donts: **Don't** colour anything that is not reporting agent work, operator ownership, an error, a link, code syntax or an agent family's identity; no decorative accents or coloured side rails.
**Don't** pulse, breathe or animate a shadow; the only glow is a lit pane's bloom (The Bloom Rule) and the only blinking element is the streaming cursor pane, which stops under reduced motion.
**Don't** add scanlines, HUD chrome, letterspaced uppercase labels, eyebrows or kickers above headings; labels are sentence case.

**Don't** use glass, blur or decorative gradients; depth is tonal value plus the edge light, the room's ambient light is the one gradient, the bloom is the one zero-offset shadow, and only floating surfaces cast an offset shadow.
**Don't** draw a border around a plate; borders belong to inputs, outline buttons and hairline dividers.
**Don't** replace a pane with a dot, a circle, a badge or a glyph icon, and never make colour the only signal.
**Don't** use Geist for headings, labels or buttons, or a system display face anywhere.
**Don't** round panels or shell surfaces beyond 4px, or reintroduce the Classic skin's rounded panels and amber accents into the Nerve style.
**Don't** put pills, dots or badges on a task card for priority, status or run state; the pane and a word carry it.
